draft.title: What a business is
card: A business makes and sells goods or services. Goods are things you can touch. Services are things done for you.
Businesses exist to meet people's needs and wants. Needs are things people must have, such as food. Wants are things people would like, such as a new game.
Many businesses aim to make a profit. Profit is the money left after the business pays its costs.
Businesses also give people jobs. Workers earn money by helping the business run.
draft.remember: A business sells goods or services to meet needs and wants, earn a profit and create jobs.

a.q: Which of these is a business?
opts: A bakery that sells bread to local families
A family that bakes bread for its own dinner
A school that lends books to its students
A friend who gives away cakes at a party
a.why: The bakery makes bread and sells it to customers. The family bakes only for itself, so it sells nothing. Giving things away or lending them is not selling.
a.clue: A business sells what it makes.

b.q: Tom opens a bike repair shop in Hobart. He hires two workers. Which reason for a business does hiring them show?
opts: Giving people jobs
Making a profit
Meeting a need
Selling a good
b.why: Hiring workers gives people jobs, which is one reason businesses exist. Profit is the money left after costs, and hiring workers does not show that. Repairs may meet a need, but the hiring is about jobs.
b.clue: Think about what the two workers receive.

a.best: A bakery that sells bread to local families

problems.detail: The card defines goods ('things you can touch') and services ('things done for you'), which is point 2 (Goods and services). This point should only mention goods and services, not explain them.

The remember line says a business sells to 'earn a profit', which suggests every business does. The card only says many businesses aim to make a profit. The remember line should keep the card's hedge, for example 'aim to make a profit'.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer. The card defines goods and services, which belong to point 2, and the remember line says businesses earn a profit where the card only says many aim to.
